title: No barber shaves exactly those who do not shave themselves
statement: For any binary relation `shaves` on any domain, there is no element b such that for every x, b shaves x if and only if x does not shave x.

formal.statement: (assert (not (exists ((b Person)) (forall ((x Person)) (= (shaves b x) (not (shaves x x)))))))

provenance.source: authored from the S:logic-and-proof strand of the math-education concept graph; statement written here, not copied

notes: OPEN IN THIS LEDGER, NOT IN MATHEMATICS. axeyum gets the right VERDICT and no usable evidence, which is a more interesting failure than returning `unknown`. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-barber-no-such-barber.smt2`: it printed `; evidence kind=unsat-drat certified=0 recheck=na arena=FAIL ms=171` and then `unsat`. Read that line carefully, because two of its fields WERE misreported by the harness rather than by the solver -- both are now fixed; see the 2026-08-17 update at the end. The evidence object is a BARE `Evidence::Unsat(None)` -- no certificate at all -- but `Evidence::kind_label` maps every `Unsat` variant to the string `unsat-drat`, so the line names a DRAT proof that does not exist; and `Evidence::check` returns `Ok(false)` for a bare unsat, which the CLI renders as `arena=FAIL`, i.e. as though a certificate had been examined and found wanting. `Evidence::check_outcome` on the same input correctly answers `NothingToCheck(UncertifiedUnsat)`. The verdict is right, the certificate is absent, and the status here stays `open` because an uncertified unsat is not evidence under this schema. The proposition is one universal instantiation (x := b) away from the already-proved F:no-self-negating-proposition. [CORRECTED 2026-08-17: the second half of this sentence previously read `but that instantiation step is one no component of ours performed or recorded`, and that is FALSE -- see the reconstruction trace in the update below.] UPDATE 2026-08-17: the two harness misreports above are REPAIRED, re-measured with the same command: it now prints `; evidence kind=unsat-uncertified certified=0 recheck=na arena=none:uncertified-unsat`. `Evidence::kind_label` now distinguishes the variants (`crates/axeyum-solver/src/evidence.rs:725-726`: `Unsat(Some(_)) => "unsat-drat"`, `Unsat(None) => "unsat-uncertified"`), so the line no longer names a DRAT proof that does not exist, and `arena=FAIL` -- which read as though a certificate had been examined and rejected -- is now `arena=none:uncertified-unsat`, which says there was nothing to examine. The SUBSTANCE is unchanged: right verdict, no certificate, status stays `open`. What changed on this date is that the gap is now GATED rather than merely recorded. `scripts/check-smt-evidence-certified.py` requires every settled smt-term-level / smt-clausal fact to report `certified=1` (measured: 17 of 17 do), because the evidence commands those facts carry test only the VERDICT -- `test "$(... | tail -1)" = unsat` passes on an uncertified refutation, verified against this very instance. This instance is that check's negative control: genuinely unsat so a verdict-only checker accepts it, genuinely uncertified so a certification-aware one must not. If it ever reports `certified=1` the check FAILS on purpose, saying that this fact can now be closed and the control must be repointed. RECONSTRUCTION TRACE 2026-08-17 (measured, `AXEYUM_QTRACE=1`): the solver DOES perform and DOES record the instantiation. `auto::solve` skolemizes the top existential to `!sk_0`, then the e-graph route (`prove_quantified_unsat_via_egraph`) admits exactly one instance -- the universal at the existential's own Skolem witness -- and `check_auto` refutes the resulting `p = not p`. That instance is recorded as a `QuantifierInstanceCertificate` (`crates/axeyum-solver/src/qinst_egraph.rs:2737`) which already has a PUBLIC independent checker, `check_quantifier_ground_derivation` (:2821). It is simply never plumbed out: the certificates live in a function-local `ground_derivations` map (:1162) that dies at each `return Ok(Unsat)`, `skolemize_top_existentials` (`auto.rs:889`) returns `Vec<TermId>` and discards the assertion-to-`!sk_k` correspondence, and `evidence.rs` references neither (grep: 0 hits). `prove_unsat_to_lean` declines at `skolem_alethe.rs:102-105`, whose slice requires the existential's body to be a single quantifier-free equality; the barber's body is a universal, so both conjuncts fail. So this is NOT a proposition whose refutation is unreconstructable -- it is one where the reconstruction path re-derives the instantiation from scratch with a strictly weaker vocabulary (witness search reads only the ground partition, and `b` occurs only under the binder) and a strictly weaker ground gate (congruence-only, needing exactly one disequality, which `p = not p` does not have). Measured control: the fully instantiated ground formula `(= (shaves b b) (not (shaves b b)))` DOES reconstruct kernel-checked today. Only the instantiation step is missing.
